DOCUMENTATION

Selection criteria

Include a report when it supplies traceable evidence for a concrete MOD business-case question. Record what it can support and what it cannot.

Policy v1.0 · effective 17 September 2026. Apply all eight criteria to each candidate and record the judgement against its stable report ID. There is no numerical quality score: relevance, access and methodological strength are different things.

Selection gates

CriterionInclusion ruleConditional inclusion or rejection
C1 · MOD relevanceA defence programme, capability or enabling function, with an explicit MOD decision use and at least one business-case dimension.A civilian or cross-government comparator needs a plausible transfer mechanism and a stated contextual boundary. Exclude if the connection is merely topical.
C2 · Completed evidenceA completed process, impact, value-for-money, formative or developmental evaluation; or a performance/value-for-money audit with substantive findings.Audit-body factual investigations may qualify only for a specific cost, control or delivery question, with their restricted scope prominent. Exclude strategies, evaluation plans, announcements, opinion, routine accounts and technical equipment trials without programme-level learning.
C3 · Credible, identifiable sourceAn identifiable report and issuing/evaluating organisation, with a public primary-source publication or report link and a date at the available precision.Official summaries may qualify under C4. Hold unverifiable or inaccessible claims until the source can be established. Publisher identity alone does not establish methodological quality.
C4 · Appraisable, traceable evidenceThe summary identifies the question, methods or evidence basis, findings, limitations and locators. Recommendations are included if present; absence is stated.Official summaries, extracts, highlights and analyst translations require a visible access/translation limit. Obtain fuller methods or language review for decision-critical claims. Hold material too thin to support even a bounded lesson.
C5 · Decision usefulnessState one concrete use for testing options, assumptions, costs, benefits, risk, procurement or delivery. Findings must go beyond a description of the programme.Audit findings must support a specified decision; generic institutional commentary is insufficient. Exclude if no usable finding can be identified.
C6 · Honest interpretationSeparate source findings, source recommendations and analyst inference. Match claims to the design. Preserve scope, sampling, timing, attribution and transfer limits.Do not present a recommendation as proof, a before/after change as a causal estimate, a cost forecast as a benefit, or an audit as an impact evaluation. Hold unsupported wording until corrected.
C7 · Distinct and applicableOne record per report/version; identify related studies, shared cases and later reports. Check whether the mechanism and context remain useful.Prioritise recent evidence when equally useful. Reports over five years old need an explicit continuing use and timing boundary; reports over eight years old require a recorded exception. Exclude duplicate formats; retain earlier editions only where they add a distinct period or finding.
C8 · Concise and completeA readable title, date, type, country, decision use, findings, methods, source links/locators, MOD relevance and evidence limits. Keep each narrative field to approximately 25–60 words where possible; use a single sentence for the decision use.Store longer provenance separately. “Not reported” or a documented absence is preferable to invention. Hold materially incomplete summaries; correct classification and metadata errors before inclusion.

Decision rule

  • Include: all gates pass for the stated use. Normal study and transfer limitations still apply.
  • Include with limits: the report has a useful, traceable application but an explicit exception applies under C1, C2, C4 or C7. Record the reason and put the boundary in the interface.
  • Hold: relevance is plausible but the source, extraction, methods or claim needs work. Retain in the editorial ledger; omit from evidence results until resolved.
  • Exclude: outside scope, unsupported, unusable or duplicate. Retain the screening reason; do not silently delete its history.

“Pass” in the content review means the editorial gate is met for the proposed use. It is not a finding that the study has low risk of bias. “Conditional” identifies a documented exception. Country, source access and inclusion labels must never substitute for appraisal of a particular claim.

Audit relevance test

An audit qualifies when its empirical findings help assess an option, a cost or benefit assumption, a delivery dependency, a commercial arrangement or a control. A finding that governance was weak can justify a risk mitigation or assurance question; it does not establish the impact of the proposed remedy.

Factual investigations are labelled separately. For example, the Afghanistan Response Route informs cost traceability, while military support for Ukraine informs resource demands. The NAO explicitly limits the evaluative scope of both reports: ARR source scope; Ukraine source scope.

Minimum checks before adoption in a business case

Read the relevant original passage. Check the intervention, population, comparator, setting, period, method and outcome. For a monetary or impact assumption, inspect the estimate, uncertainty, price base, counterfactual and transfer conditions. The catalogue does not currently extract standardised effect sizes, confidence intervals or cost bases; consult the source before using a quantitative estimate.

Method choices should answer the decision question. Process, impact and value-for-money evaluation provide different kinds of information, as described in the Magenta Book. These editorial checks are proportionate discovery aids, not a substitute for source appraisal.
